why: The relink queue lived only in handoff/PLAN-E2-C-relink-v3.md, in prose with checkboxes, and it was wrong twice: 3b was recorded as written into the tree when grep found zero hits, and item 8 said 'both places were fixed' when only one was. Both were caught by a human audit, and a human audit does not run itself on the day of the link. This file is the same queue as data, so tools/check_relink_queue.py can run it. P1 complete is the condition for linking; missing one item means a second relink.
expectationSemantics: `present` means the item is done and must stay done. `absent` means the item is NOT done and the tree must not quietly acquire it either -- an item that appears without its expectation being flipped is drift in the direction nobody audits. Flipping an expectation is a deliberate edit and shows up in the diff.

items.title: the containment reorder -- NOT in this link (2026-08-16, measured): it would change no disputed cell
items.note: Measured off the frozen engine: on the disputed cells containment is checked and HELD (selection 1807-2471, restore centre 1945). Reordering it ahead of multiBlock therefore changes nothing there. This retreat condition was named by external adjudication before the data existed. The real defect is different and is filed separately: .uno:SelectText overshoots an empty paragraph, so the barrier refuses a mutation that succeeded -- and containment cannot catch that, because it asks whether the selection COVERS the caret, never whether it covers ONLY the caret's paragraph.

items.title: the engine must report its WASM heap in the typed state -- WITHDRAWN 2026-08-16, measured
items.note: Withdrawn, not deferred.  The figure is already reachable on the shipped artifact (engine prints it every stage, worker forwards it under `debug`, SDK already accepts `debug`), and emscripten_get_heap_size() is a constant 1073741824 because every profile links -sTOTAL_MEMORY=1GB without ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH -- so the field would have carried a number that cannot move, and d4-memory's slope criterion would have passed on it forever. The moving figure is `sbrk`, on the same stage line. Evidence: findings/evidence/sdk-e2/e2-c-validation/d4/heap/. The check below stays `absent` deliberately: nothing should acquire this field quietly now that it is known to be the wrong one.

items.note: Same family as P1 item 3 (the route field). Fixed by saying so rather than by guessing: the counts keep their type and value, and preBlocksObserved/postBlocksObserved say whether the value is one. Worker projects both, plus readbackParsed, readbackBlockCount and containment{checked,held} -- the fields 3b's criterion needs and the field that says whether the verdict is about the caller's paragraph at all. Engine change is object-compiled only (scratch dir, never a profile build dir); it enters the artifact at the relink.

This is finding 046's actual defect, now precise. Raw readback on the empty paragraph: `

E1-EMPTY-AFTER

Not blocking this link: the fix needs a design (verify by block identity rather than refuse) plus its own measurement, and the link is for changes already decided. blocksRelinkSemantics: An item with blocksRelink true must be AS-DECLARED **and**, if it is declared absent, it is still outstanding work -- so P1 is not complete while it is open. Two items are deliberately false: the WASM heap field was withdrawn after measurement (2026-08-16), and the search-after-reopen wedge is an observation the product does not take today. Without this field the checker would report 'P1 complete' whenever every finished item was finished, which is the exact shape of a check that agrees with whatever it is shown.
externalAdjudication2026_08_16: fable, called as a subagent, refuted the premise that the two remaining blockers cannot be measured before the relink. Verified independently, all three claims: (1) tools/build_e2_discovery_profile.py COPIES the wasm (shutil.copy2, --wasm is an input), so a diagnostic profile can be packaged around the frozen 572035ac bytes -- no engine build, same engine; (2) the frozen wasm already serialises "readback":{"parsed": / "blockCount": / "itemCount": / "html":" and "containment":{"checked": (one occurrence each; "preBlocksObserved": zero, correct -- that is today's unlinked change); (3) all six worker patch anchors match exactly once in the FROZEN dist worker. Consequence: 3b's criterion and the containment ordering are both measurable now, for the price of a Python repackage plus browser rounds. Linking before that measurement would risk a v4, which costs the whole E2-B rerun plus E2-C D0-D5 again.
